item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
"there's a fundamental disconnect with the way charities work" -> An anomalous charity will not work "like a charity", in the same sense that the GOC does not operate as a peacekeeping force, the Foundation does not operate as a scientific institute / transnac or Wondertainment is not an international toys seller. Multiple charities connected to MCF do work like charities, openly, with a public face; whoever gets to this hub, however, will be getting far more than the general public. They'll be getting a way to join and / or learn more about the MCF and anomalies, because (this incarnation of) MCF cannot openly reveal their anomalous operations to civilians.

Um… no? The Foundation is not and has never been a scientific institute. It's clearly a paranoid prison system layered in bureaucracy. Furthermore, the GOI and the Foundation design schemes reflect what the organizations are supposed to be doing. The GOI, Clef's tale hub, abandon the pretense of being part of the UN by adopting a stance that makes me think that it isn't an occult peacekeeping organization. The Foundation is clearly a giant, secret bureaucracy that keeps scary things hidden away, both in terms of the SCP article format, the nomenclature and the language used on the site. Manna doesn't smell like any kind of charity at all. I would not believe for a second that they were actually doing things to help the world.

This is a hub where certain individuals that may eventually become part of the MCF get. It's not meant for everyone. It's meant for those who dug deep enough as to get here, for those desperate enough to simply keep searching for a better way to change things for those who are poor, the destitute, entire regions that have literally no way to fend for themselves but outside humanitarian aid… or conspiranoid buffs, of course. Only certain people get here, the rest are fed It's not meant for those who just want to give money to the MCF or to NGOs related to it; "civilians" get misinformation because the MCF is supposed to keep their anomalous activities quiet among the citizenship of the industrialized world, where other organisations for control of the anomalous are more deeply rooted and influential. This data is meant for those who want to learn about the ways to exploit anomalies for humankind's "healing".

So give me the misinformation. I don't want or need to see the "super secret hub". It detracts from the idea that this is a charity or an NGO. When building up the brand identity of the Hand we used secret communications and clandestine stuff because that's the only thing that the Hand is. By taking the hub and making it the "super secret" part of the Manna you lose what it is that makes this GOI unique, that they have a public facing charity that actually interacts with the public. By choosing to go "sooper sekret" you've lost a facet of what could make Manna interesting.

I get what you mean, I didn't realize until well into the contest and frankly… why wouldn't it? This page is meant, as mentioned, for those people desperate enough to help others as to seek empowerment and options on anomalies… but for some of those who get here, the revelation that anomalies are practically everywhere is going to be earth-shattering. Going with the "Matrix Approach" does not read as a far-fetched approach, nor a particularly horrible choice.

I dunno. The Matrix approach seems "hack" and overdone at this point. It doesn't inspire me with confidence that the organization takes itself seriously. Who in 2014 is going to choose a neon-green "courier new" style for anything outside of a genre piece? The best secrets look innocuous, they don't look like they're trying to be secret.

I should also point out that listing all the projects, donors and mission statements in weird, bureaucratic language is a terrible idea even for the "desperate do gooders". What is a do gooder supposed to think if they stumble here? That they accidentally hacked into somebody's secure files? That somebody was dumb enough to leave secure files out here for any rando to find? That they've run into somebody's Augmented Reality game or hobby project from the 90s?

Besides, the MCF (in this incarnation, at least) does not want conspiranoids joining their ranks; just people who have been branded by the worse this world has to offer and their response is to help those in need by doing whatever they can.

People like that don't go off looking for crazy, secret, 90s portrayal of hacker charities on the web. They look for existing groups with obvious public faces or start their own. You've put together a page for crazy hacker conspiranoids and are expecting the Peace Corps to emerge from it. That's not a good policy.

item.content:encoded:
Starting new response message to differentiate from previous response.

Firstly, I apologize for the migraine. I did not consider that possibility and, honestly, only wanted to make it look vibrant, not an extra-colorful trigger (have Horton's myself). I promise I'll be reviewing the color scheme for the MCF GOI_format and contest tales in the next week (namely, as soon as I can). About the design issue:

  • I did have several simplified presentations of a green-white scheme, but they always included bright green; what they did not include was "easy-to-read sans serifs", which could be considered, of course, nor "glossy photos", because I discarded the idea of adding photos early in the design phase. That is another questionable design choice, true.
  • The "cool, non threatening colors" part, frankly, I don't care for. I will reduce the brightness of all colors, but it's gonna be green (darker) and white.
  • And about "public-facing FAQs that are simple and non-threatening", read down. But I must admit "or if this is just bad, intrusive design." is a strong reason why this page just doesn't work good enough; I have literally zero idea about design. I did base the writing on this page on DWB's FAQ and statutes, though.

Second: to the more specific points of interest.

  • "there's a fundamental disconnect with the way charities work" -> An anomalous charity will not work "like a charity", in the same sense that the GOC does not operate as a peacekeeping force, the Foundation does not operate as a scientific institute / transnac or Wondertainment is not an international toys seller. Multiple charities connected to MCF do work like charities, openly, with a public face; whoever gets to this hub, however, will be getting far more than the general public. They'll be getting a way to join and / or learn more about the MCF and anomalies, because (this incarnation of) MCF cannot openly reveal their anomalous operations to civilians.
  • "Nothing about this encourages me to donate or put mu trust in this organization." This is a hub where certain individuals that may eventually become part of the MCF get. It's not meant for everyone. It's meant for those who dug deep enough as to get here, for those desperate enough to simply keep searching for a better way to change things for those who are poor, the destitute, entire regions that have literally no way to fend for themselves but outside humanitarian aid… or conspiranoid buffs, of course. Only certain people get here, the rest are fed It's not meant for those who just want to give money to the MCF or to NGOs related to it; "civilians" get misinformation because the MCF is supposed to keep their anomalous activities quiet among the citizenship of the industrialized world, where other organisations for control of the anomalous are more deeply rooted and influential. This data is meant for those who want to learn about the ways to exploit anomalies for humankind's "healing".
  • "It looks like it was stolen from The Matrix." I get what you mean, I didn't realize until well into the contest and frankly… why wouldn't it? This page is meant, as mentioned, for those people desperate enough to help others as to seek empowerment and options on anomalies… but for some of those who get here, the revelation that anomalies are practically everywhere is going to be earth-shattering. Going with the "Matrix Approach" does not read as a far-fetched approach, nor a particularly horrible choice.
    • Besides, the MCF (in this incarnation, at least) does not want conspiranoids joining their ranks; just people who have been branded by the worse this world has to offer and their response is to help those in need by doing whatever they can. Those people come and stay. The rest get back to their home countries after a tour, usually with mild amnestics that reinforce their Denial of Disbelief ("If It's Too Strange To Believe It, I'll Refuse To Believe It").

Anyways, again: I'm very sorry that you didn't like the contents and that the page theme obliterated any chance you had to read them in peace; I'll get that sorted out, I swear. Once I have a new theme, I'll warn you as soon as I can so you can confirm me whether or not it's tolerable.

(Thank you and sorry again.)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: The color scheme and font make this impossible to read for me. The entire thing is a migraine trigger. I'm not being hyperbolic either. I literally have been diagnosed with migraines and these pages are unreadable. Furthermore, none of the design philosophy makes sense for a charity. Nothing about this encourages me to donate or put mu trust in this organization. It's not friendly or welcoming or easy to read. It looks like it was stolen from The Matrix. national charities use easy-to-read sans serifs glossy photos and cool, non-threatening colors with public-facing FAQs that are simple and non-threatening. I can't tell if these issues are part of a broader theme that this team puts forward for Manna or if it's just because there's a fundamental disconnect with the way charities work or if this is just bad, intrusive design. I'll never know because I can't read these pages without triggering an aura migraine.
